name: Network Null Model
summary: Generates an esemble of networks according to null models that try to reproduce the data. Erdos reyni (random), Barabási-Albert and Configuration model are implemented

outputs.description: Network file containing the realizations of the null-model.

parameters.description: Number of null model samples to be generated.

Model to generate the null samples.
- random: ER network with same number of nodes and edges as the original network.
- barabasi: Scale-free model with similar number of nodes and edges as the original network.
- configuration: Generates a network with same (or similar) degree sequence as the original.

options.label: Erdős–Rényi (Random)
options.description: ER network with same number of nodes and edges as the original network.

options.label: Barabási–Albert (scale-free)
options.description: Scale-free model with similar number of nodes and edges as the original network.

options.label: Configuration
options.description: Generates a network with same (or similar) degree sequence as the original.

options.label: Ignore
options.description: Weights are ignored and the output models are unweighted.

options.label: Sample
options.description: Samples the weights from the original weights in order to maintain weight distribution.

options.label: Average
options.description: All weights have the average weight of the original network.

parameters.description:
If configuration model is selected, this selects the method to be used.
- Simple:  The generated null model may have self loops and multiple edges.
- No self-loops and multiple edges: Avoids creating self-loops and multiple edges. (Much slower than "simple")
- Monte-Carlo: Uses Monte-Carlo method to randomize the networks. Based on the Fabien Viger's method.
